newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks recoup some losses, NYSE lifts curbs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks recoup some losses, NYSE lifts curbs.

text.p: Wall Street shares recouped some early-session losses but remained weak in choppy trade Monday as investors digested several key earnings reports.

The Dow Jones Industrial average was off around 30 points at 7861 after falling over 50 points earlier. The New York Stock Exchange set index-arbitrage trading curbs at 0947 EDT/1347 GMT, then lifted them seven minutes later.
The Nasdaq composite was down eight points at 1540.
"We are seeing some follow-through profit-taking from Friday's session," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.

The market was also focused on second quarter earnings results from International Business Machines Corp, due after the market close, and a speech by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan scheduled for Tuesday.
"The market will probably be choppy in anticipation of Greenspan's speech," Crane said.
The Fed chief delivers his semi-annual testimony to the House Banking Subcommittee tomorrow, and markets would watch for any words on inflation or interest rates, analysts said.
